originality.rationale: Known exact k-matching H-descriptions (Torres all bipartite and Gill–Linusson complete bipartite) are correctly treated as inputs, not new. The new subject is intrinsic standard-Euclidean inball radius and full center locus for arbitrary connected simple biregular p<q supports, including the cycle-rank center dimension and sparse-incidence transition. Resultary returned related graph-polytope inradius phases, root/symmetric edge polytopes, and a square-assignment incenter indexed result but no broader exact biregular sparse matching center theorem. A plausible unindexed graph-supported transportation incenter characterization is an explicit risk.
residual_risks: An unindexed transportation-polytope incenter theorem covering graph-supported capacity caps could logically subsume the sparse classification.
Square Birkhoff incenter indexed result was available as a summary rather than full text.
The LP checker is numerical and cannot alone validate universal equations or delicate equality boundaries.

value.rationale: A parameter-sharp geometric classification on arbitrary connected biregular graph supports distinguishes unique center from graph cycle-space transportation families. The incidence(K4) to incidence(K5) exact same-radius but nonunique-to-unique collapse makes a motivated sparse-support phase transition, not a gratuitous finite table.

limitations: Simple connected p<q biregular graphs, k from 1 to p; exclude equal-side, irregular support and alternative Euclidean rescalings.
Supporting hyperplanes need not all be facets in sparse graphs; no assertion that they are.
